details:
@azure-growth/signup-ux-components 1.2.2, 1.2.3 and 2.9.9 are dependency-confusion packages that take the name of a package used internally by Microsoft's Azure signup site and not published on the npm registry; 2.9.9 carries a version number above the internal release, so resolvers that also check the public registry prefer it. Their `preinstall` script runs `node index.js`, which reads the OS username and hostname and sends them in a DNS lookup of `msrc-poc.<user>.<hostname>.dbg6vplohjpkmtolbi6g18ekofkxjzm4s.oast.fun`, an out-of-band interaction collector; `index.js` is also the package entry point, so the lookup repeats whenever the package is required. Any machine that installed one of these versions has disclosed its username and hostname to a third party. The earlier `0.0.0-stage` version is an inert placeholder and is not affected.

## Source: amazon-inspector (abe2b01490162d3d9f3330f7e49a1960841d24c5007ec1734f82b23480e4c769)
On npm install, the package's preinstall lifecycle hook executes index.js, which reads the installer's OS username (os.userInfo().username) and hostname (os.hostname()) and embeds them as labels in a subdomain under an interactsh out-of-band collector (dbg6vplohjpkmtolbi6g18ekofkxjzm4s.oast.fun), then triggers a DNS resolution for that name. The resulting DNS query transmits the installer's identity to the attacker-controlled DNS listener. The @azure-growth scope impersonates Microsoft/Azure internal naming, consistent with a dependency-confusion probe targeting an internal Azure package. The package provides no legitimate UI-component functionality to justify this behavior.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (d6aa62a9421f736418e09f0b247beb52637c7cb21f03cfba35656222e48215fc)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified '@azure-growth/signup-ux-components' @ 1.2.2 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.
